question: persister
constraint: using live-cell imaging as the only readout
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out using live-cell imaging as the only readout. Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment fate prediction with lineage-tracked cell-cycle and death reporters
ideas.description: Co-express a FUCCI cell-cycle reporter and a caspase-3/7 biosensor, then image the same cells for 24-48 h before and after drug addition. Trace each cell's lineage backward from its eventual fate to ask whether cell-cycle phase, division history, or time since last mitosis before treatment predicts survival.

ideas.title: Live kinase-translocation reporters to find pre-existing signaling states
ideas.description: Use ERK and AKT kinase translocation reporters (KTRs) to measure pathway activity in each cell before the inhibitor is added and then track it through treatment. Test whether survivors had a distinct baseline signaling level or pulse dynamics, and whether that difference is stable across generations.

ideas.title: Metabolic and organelle reporters for pre-existing survival states
ideas.description: Image membrane potential (TMRM or similar dye), an ATP or NADH/NAD+ biosensor such as Peredox, and mitochondrial mass in single cells over time. Compare these baseline and early-treatment metabolic profiles between eventual survivors and dying cells to identify a metabolic signature that precedes survival.

ideas.title: Pulse-washout and reseeding kinetics to separate reversible tolerance from heritable resistance
ideas.description: Apply the drug as a timed pulse, wash it out, and track survivors for several generations in drug-free medium using time-lapse imaging. Measure whether they regain normal proliferation and whether their progeny keep the tolerant phenotype, which separates reversible drug-tolerant states from stable, heritable resistance.

ideas.title: Label-free morphology and motility classifier for predicting survival
ideas.description: Record phase-contrast or brightfield time-lapse of the untreated population and extract single-cell features such as shape, texture, speed, and persistence. Train a classifier on the fates observed after treatment, then validate it on held-out cells and by live-sorting predicted survivors for follow-up.
